keySentence: Mowgli existed between two worlds — belonging fully to neither the jungle nor the village.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli's story is about growing up between two worlds. He had the instincts of a jungle animal and the body of a boy. Each world gave him something real but held something back. The jungle gave him freedom but not his full humanity. The village gave him humanity but not the wildness he needed. He walked the line between them without fully crossing either. This is not only a sad story but also a rich one about border lives. Mowgli existed between two worlds — belonging fully to neither the jungle nor the village.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli's story is really a story about what happens when you grow up between two different worlds. He had the instincts of a jungle animal and the intelligence and form of a human being. Each world offered him something real and each world also withheld something from him. The jungle gave him freedom and belonging but could not give him his full humanity. The village gave him his humanity but could not give him the wildness that had made him who he was. He spent much of his life walking the line between these two worlds without fully crossing either. This is not entirely a sad story — it is also a story about the richness of living at the border. Mowgli existed between two worlds — belonging fully to neither the jungle nor the village.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli's story, read carefully, is really the story of what happens to a human being who grows up permanently between two different worlds. He had the sharpened instincts of a jungle animal combined with the reasoning mind and physical form of a young human being. Each of the two worlds he inhabited offered him something real and important — and each of the two worlds also withheld something equally real from him. The jungle gave him freedom, belonging, a sense of wild competence, and a family of wolves who loved him without condition — but it could not give him his full humanity. The human village gave him his humanity, a place in recorded history, a language with words for abstract things — but it could not give him the wildness that had made him into who he was. He spent most of his life walking carefully along the line between these two worlds, without ever fully crossing over into either one and settling down. This is not entirely a tragic story, despite how it might first appear to readers who prefer clean endings and clear resolutions. It is also a story about the particular richness of lives lived at borders, and about the things that only someone with Mowgli's specific history can actually see clearly. Mowgli existed between two worlds — belonging fully to neither the jungle nor the village.
